source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-26: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 26 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: For Variant 26, assume a specified multi-node GPU workload, topology, NIC/link, GPU-direct capability, driver, framework, transport, and fallback configuration; record these rather than infer them. RDMA can move data through the application collective or point-to-point operation, communication library, verbs objects (queue pairs, work requests and completions), registered memory and access permissions, NIC and link, and remote memory or GPU buffer before synchronization and completion. Explain whether the observed path is GPU-direct/zero-copy or host-staged, and identify conditions that force fallback. Define a falsifiable hypothesis against a named non-RDMA baseline, including message-size and batch/parallelism distributions, rank/topology cases, warm-up, steady-state window, repetitions, clock source, and units. Measure application end-to-end and per-operation communication time, GPU step time and overlap, throughput, latency percentiles, CPU use, completion/error counters, retransmissions or link events when available, and relevant device counters; correlate them without treating any counter as proof of user-visible benefit. Analyze congestion, NUMA/PCIe placement, caching, power state, software versions, overlap, and workload mix as confounders, report uncertainty, and separate measurements from estimates. For the required link-failure case, specify detection, classification, bounded retry/timeout behavior, health checks, correctness checks, and a safe fallback or rollback trigger; never silently continue with corrupted or unverified data. Require failure-injection evidence, reproducible baseline/RDMA runs, correlated application and device traces, and privacy review before enabling the change or claiming improvement. Do not invent platform facts, expose credentials, or publish sensitive telemetry.

device/link counters can diverge from end-to-end application behavior
fallback and retries can hide faults or alter timing
telemetry can disclose sensitive infrastructure details
evidence_required: hardware/software/topology and transport configuration capture
same-workload repeated baseline and RDMA measurements with uncertainty
correlated application traces, completion data, and device/link counters
failure-injection results covering detection, recovery, correctness, and rollback
privacy review of collected telemetry
